label: eComms
title: Archiving & Supervision
intro: Capture every channel your firm uses, then supervise it with a risk graph you configure yourself — AI rules and lexicons working together, cutting false positives by 99.14% and leaving a reviewable trail behind every decision.
headline: Every channel,
one record.

blocks.text: Email, chat, text, voice, and social — captured where your people actually talk, then written once to a WORM, 17a-4 compliant record that supervision, review, and exams all read from.
Supervision runs on a risk graph you configure — combining AI rules and lexicons, so what gets escalated reflects your program, not a vendor’s default keyword list.

label: People
title: Employee Compliance
intro: Personal trading, gifts and entertainment, outside business activities, and attestations in one place — with reminders your team will actually act on.
headline: Every person,
one regulatory profile.

blocks.text: Trading, gifts, outside activities, and attestations all hang off the same employee record — so you see one person’s full picture instead of six disconnected spreadsheets.
Requests are pre-cleared against your restricted lists in seconds, reminders go out where people already work, and every approval writes itself to the record.

label: Program
title: Firm Compliance
intro: Every process, risk, and control mapped and documented in one place — built as workflows with Go Agents doing the monitoring, so the calendar and the evidence keep themselves current.
headline: No more spreadsheets.
No more clunky calendars.

blocks.text: Every compliance process, risk, and control — mapped, documented, and connected to the program it belongs to, so nothing lives in someone’s tab or someone’s head.
Build each process as a workflow, drop a Go Agent into any step to do the watching and the drafting, and let the evidence write itself as the work happens.

label: 3rd party risk
title: Third-Party Diligence
intro: Onboard and re-review every third party you rely on — questionnaires drafted from the web and their own documents, risk ratings set by your team, and the whole file kept with the rest of your records.
headline: Intelligent questionnaire
and risk automation.

blocks.text: Go pulls from the public web, the documents a counterparty sends you, and last year’s review, then drafts every answer with the source attached — so the questionnaire arrives mostly finished.
Your team reviews what actually needs judgment, sets the risk rating, and the whole file — evidence, findings, sign-off — lands in your records on a re-review schedule.

label: Reviews
title: Content Reviews
intro: One integrated workflow from first draft to exam file — Go pre-reviews content wherever creators work, your team runs the review process you configure, and every version, flag, and approval is preserved.
headline: Pre-review and post-review,
one workflow.

blocks.text: {go} catches the obvious problems before anything reaches your queue, and everything that does arrive comes with its history intact.

items.title: Pre-review, wherever the work happens
items.text: Creators ask Go for feedback from Slack, Teams, or the browser and get it against your policies, your past decisions, and the rules — then submit for review from the same conversation, by chat or MCP.

items.title: A review process you configure
items.text: Set your own stages, reviewer questions, and approval logic. Reviewers see Go’s flags with the rule cited, leave comments on the piece, and route it onward — nothing leaves the system.

items.title: Exam production in a click
items.text: Every version, comment, flag, and approval stays attached to the piece, so producing the file for an exam is a query rather than a week of assembly.

label: Recordkeeping
title: Unified Books & Records
intro: One WORM-based, 17a-4 compliant record for the whole firm — every message, approval, and attestation captured as it happens, so an exam request is a search instead of a scramble across vendors.
headline: Exam-ready, the day
it happens.

blocks.text: Most firms keep their records in five systems and rebuild the file when a request arrives. Here every action — a supervised message, an attestation, a pre-clearance, a content approval, a vendor file — writes to one WORM-based, 17a-4 compliant record the moment it happens.

items.text: Produce a complete, timestamped file for a deficiency letter or sweep in minutes, not the weeks it takes to pull exports from separate vendors and stitch them together.
One record means no gaps, no duplicates, and no arguing about which system is authoritative when two of them disagree.
Every entry carries who did it, when, under which policy version, and what they saw — so you can show a control operated, not just that it existed.
WORM storage and 17a-4 retention are enforced by the architecture, so nothing can be quietly edited or deleted after the fact.

blocks.text: Because it’s one record on modern data infrastructure, it’s searchable by your team and callable by {go} — ask for every communication with a client over two years and get the file, not a project.

label: Trust
title: Privacy & Security
intro: SOC 2 Type 2 controls, granular permissions, and smarter supervision methods that protect the firm without invasive oversight of your people.
headline: Protect the firm,
respect your people.

blocks.text: SOC 2 Type 2 controls and permissions down to the individual record mean everyone sees exactly what their role requires — and nothing more.
Supervision focuses on real risk instead of blanket surveillance, so your program stays rigorous without making your people feel watched.
